c.tagline: Where the Rhine and Moselle meet at the historic German Corner

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and reliable; ranks at the Hauptbahnhof and Altstadt, or order by phone or app

emergency.note: Emergency services are highly reliable; English is often understood by dispatchers in this well-touristed region

hood_desc: Koblenz's picturesque old town, wedged between the Rhine and Moselle rivers and centered on the Deutsches Eck monument where they merge. Cobblestone lanes, half-timbered houses, and riverside promenades make this the tourist heart of the city.

Perched on a plateau across the Rhine, this district is dominated by the massive Ehrenbreitstein Fortress, reachable by cable car with sweeping views over the river valley. Quieter and more residential than the old town below.
A student-friendly neighborhood south of the center around Görresplatz, known for its concentration of bars, pubs, and late-night eateries. The liveliest part of Koblenz after dark.
A calm riverside district along the Moselle, popular for cycling and walking paths with views back toward the fortress. Largely residential with a handful of traditional wine taverns.
The city's modern commercial core, home to the Löhr-Center shopping mall and pedestrianized shopping streets. Less historic charm but the go-to area for retail and everyday errands.

water.note: Tap water is safe and strictly regulated.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-midnight, with reduced night service on weekends
transit.pay: VRM tickets via app, machine, or contactless card; single, day, and group tickets available
transit.map: vrminfo.de journey planner and DB Navigator app
transit.note: The Altstadt and Deutsches Eck are entirely walkable; the Ehrenbreitstein cable car (Seilbahn) links the fortress across the Rhine

train: Koblenz Hauptbahnhof has direct ICE service to Frankfurt (~1 hr) and Cologne (~1 hr) on the Rhine high-speed line
bus: Flixbus and regional buses connect to major German cities
ferry: Köln-Düsseldorfer (KD) Rhine river cruises to Rüdesheim, Koblenz, and Cologne

tip.r: Round up the bill or add 5-10% in restaurants, stated verbally when paying rather than left on the table
